title: Cross-tenant soft-eviction hedging and kernel-aware orphan rehydration
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem statement:

Paged-attention workloads suffer intermittent prefill stalls and redundant decode work when KV fragments become orphaned or are evicted aggressively under cross-tenant pressure. Current eviction is largely impulse-driven (LRU-ish) and does not account for decode cost or kernel locality. This ticket implements a two-part runtime strategy: (1) cross-tenant soft-eviction hedging to reduce thrashing during short bursts, and (2) kernel-aware orphan rehydration that schedules re-population of critical KV fragments using kernel-compatible prefetch lanes. The goal is to reduce warm-start tail latency, lower redundant decode load, and improve fairness across tenants during noisy bursts.

Scope:
- Runtime allocator + eviction policy changes (soft-eviction credits, hedging window)
- Per-tenant and global admission guard to avoid starvation
- Orphan detection heuristics and kernel hint propagation for rehydration lanes
- Simulation and load-testing harness; runtime metrics and alerts

Out of scope for this ticket: persistent storage tier changes, cross-region replication, and user-facing config surface (will be added after baseline is stable).
acceptance_criteria: Simulated traces with mixed-tenant bursts show >= 35% reduction in redundant prefill decodes compared to baseline under identical memory pressure
95th percentile warm-start token latency reduced by >= 15% on benchmark trace representing chat workloads
No tenant experiences >10% increase in median latency due to hedging under typical load profiles
Runtime exposes observability: per-tenant soft-evict credits, orphan count, kernel-hint hit-rate; dashboards and alert thresholds created
Implementation covered by automated integration tests and a canary rollout plan with quantitative rollback criteria
design_notes: Soft-eviction credits: each tenant gets a small time-decayed credit bucket that absorbs N soft-evictions within a short window; credits replenish slowly based on tenant weight and historical working-set stability
Hedging window: on eviction, first attempt is a soft mark that allows reclaiming without freeing kernel-mapped slot for X ms; if pressure persists beyond hedging window the fragment is hard-evicted
Orphan detection: fragments with no active decoder references but high recent touch-frequency are marked as orphans and put into rehydration candidate list

Kernel-aware hints: when a fragment is marked for rehydration we emit a small kernel-hint object (model-id, fragment-id, byte-range, preferred kernel lane) so the kernel scheduler can coalesce rehydrations into existing decode waves
Admission control: global soft-evict budget prevents cumulative credit exhaustion leading to OOM; if exhausted, degrade to LRU with backoff and signal operators
Fairness: tenant weights used to allocate soft-evict credits; we will monitor for tenant starvation and provide emergency hard-evict override for system stability
implementation_steps: 1) Add per-tenant credit bookkeeping and hedging-window state to allocator; unit tests for credit decay and credit consumption
2) Integrate soft-mark lifecycle into page reclamation path; store soft-mark timestamp and owner-tenant metadata
3) Implement orphan detector that runs periodically and outputs rehydration candidates with estimated decode-cost score
4) Extend kernel control plane to accept kernel-hint objects and expose a 'rehydration lane' API that merges rehydrates with scheduled prefill waves
5) Add metrics: soft-evict_count, soft_eviction_credit_balance, orphan_count, kernel_hint_merge_rate, redundant_decode_count
6) Create simulator harness that replays mixed-tenant traces and measures redundant decodes and latency tail; run A/B against baseline
7) Build canary rollout with traffic shaping to limit exposure; include automatic rollback if redundant_decode_count increases or p95 latency regresses beyond threshold
8) Documentation: design doc PR to Confluence and developer-facing notes on operational knobs
tests_and_metrics: Unit tests for credit bucket math and hedging expiry
Integration test that simulates cross-tenant burst and asserts soft-evict behavior
Simulator benchmark using two synthetic traces: conversational chat and long-form generation; track redundant_decode_count and p95 token latency
Performance test: measure CPU/GPU overhead of kernel-hint plumbing (target < 1% throughput regression)
Dashboard panels: per-tenant credit balance, orphan rehydration success rate, kernel-hint merge ratio, memory churn (evictions/sec)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit and integration tests merged behind feature flag; run local simulator
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% traffic in a non-critical region; compare simulator projections vs live metrics for 48h
Phase 2 (broader canary): 25% traffic for 72h; watch fallback rates and per-tenant latency delta
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 100% on reserved fleets with full monitoring and a 4-hour automatic rollback window if alerts fire
Emergency plan: immediate disable of soft-evict and kernel-hint via runtime feature gate; fallback to baseline allocator
